issues.on_page: Operating receipts: Sales tax 4,000 (Exhibit H); the Statement of Activities counts it in proprietary Charges for Services 145,518 (p2); Sales tax paid 3,713 is printed among the expenses
issues.issue: This is sales tax collected on utility bills and passed through, not the village's own sales tax revenue. Calling it sales tax puts it next to local option sales tax. Charges for services is also defensible. The same applies to detail[44].

issues.on_page: Expenses 230,866 including Depreciation 65,041; Schedule 3 shows cash outlays not counted as expenses: principal paid 43,030 and purchase of capital assets 6,623 (p10)
issues.issue: Business-type spending is on a net position measure, so it includes non-cash depreciation and leaves out the cash paid for debt principal and capital assets. The roll-forward holds (496,360 + 146,083 - 230,866 + 69,959 = 481,536), and the extractor says this matches FY2023, but these figures are not cash disbursements.

The Street Fund capital outlay (detail[35]) got a function from its fund ('Capital Outlay: Streets/Highways'), but the General Fund one has no function. This is inconsistent, though defensible because the General Fund has no single function.
